hints.title: Forward Linked List Scan Obstacle
hints.text: Traversing forward from each node to search for a larger successor incurs O(N^2) list iterations. How can converting node values into an indexable sequence allow resolving successors for earlier nodes in amortized O(1)?

hints.title: Monotonic Decreasing Index Invariant
hints.text: Storing unresolved node indices in a decreasing sequence allows an incoming node value to immediately resolve all earlier smaller nodes.

hints.title: Index Sequence Resolution Procedure
hints.text: Traverse the linked list and collect values into an array. Initialize an answer array of size N filled with 0 and an empty index buffer. For each index i: while the buffer is non-empty and vals[i] > vals[buffer[-1]], pop index j and set answer[j] = vals[i]. Append i to the buffer. Return answer.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in linked list (1 <= N <= 10^4)
complexity.notes: Converts list to array then executes standard monotonic index resolution in linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Inner list traversals for each node take O(N^2) total operations.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Storing values in an array enables random access and strictly linear O(N) runtime.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing that linked lists lack backward traversal and indexing, making array conversion or value/index pair pushing advantageous.
